extraction.policy_summary: HUL states it has an Equal Opportunity Policy ensuring Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) are treated fairly across recruitment, career progression and workplace participation, and separately lists a distinct named 'Disability Accommodation Policy' among its Principle 3 (employee wellbeing) policies. A general equal employment opportunity policy weblink is also provided.
extraction.accommodation_process_summary: HUL states it 'encourages voluntary self-disclosure and provides tailored accommodations to support individual needs' for PWDs, and separately names a distinct 'Disability Accommodation Policy' among its HR policies, though the policy's specific content/steps are not detailed in the filing text.
extraction.pwd_employee_count_details: As of FY2025-26: 34 total differently-abled employees (33 permanent, 1 other-than-permanent) -- 24 male (70.6%), 10 female (29.4%); and 100 total differently-abled workers (98 permanent, 2 other-than-permanent) -- 89 male (89.0%), 11 female (11.0%).
extraction.physical_accessibility_measures: HUL states it has installed, in various factories and offices: ramps, lowered reception desks for wheelchair access, elevator voice annunciators, evacuation chairs, automated sliding doors, tactile flooring and Braille signage, induction loop systems, and all-gender accessible toilets, fire alarm freshers, and accessible guest rooms. Specific sites (Amli, Haridwar, R&D Centres in Mumbai and Bengaluru, and Head Office) are stated to be certified for accessibility, with a stated aim to extend certification to 100% of sites against the RPwD Act's Minimum Mandatory Standards.
extraction.recruitment_details: The filing states that through its Equal Opportunity Policy, PWDs are 'treated with fairness and dignity across recruitment, career progression, and everyday workplace participation,' and that voluntary self-disclosure is encouraged. No numeric hiring targets, attainment data, or disability-specific outreach/sourcing channels are given.
extraction.compliance_details: HUL states specific named sites are already certified for accessibility, and that it 'aims to achieve certification for 100% of our sites with the Minimum Mandatory Standards required under the Persons with Disabilities Act' -- indicating partial current attainment and a stated (not yet fully achieved) target against a specific statutory standard. No WCAG digital conformance level is claimed.
